name: Plus/minus DNA sequencing
summary: Sanger and Coulson's plus/minus method read DNA by copying it under limited-nucleotide conditions and sorting products on gels; it sequenced the φX174 genome.
description: Sanger and Coulson used primed DNA synthesis, limiting nucleotide conditions, E. coli and T4 polymerases, and gel separation to infer sequences.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

impact.note: Used mainly in one laboratory, it first allowed rapid reading of long DNA, with chain termination and one viral genome as its direct successors.

date.label: by 1974
date.basis: Demonstrations appear in a manuscript received 20 December 1974; publication followed in May 1975.

events.statement: Sanger and Coulson used primed DNA synthesis, limiting nucleotide conditions, E. coli and T4 polymerases, and gel separation to infer sequences.
events.caveats: Not the first DNA sequencing attempt; earlier primed sequencing and synthetic-primer work are explicitly mentioned by the paper and remain backlog.

links.statement: The plus/minus assay requires complementary template copying because its sequence readout comes from primer-extension products.
links.scope: The specific Sanger–Coulson primed-synthesis assay submitted in 1974.
links.alternatives: Chemical-cleavage sequencing is a different route; no all-sequencing dependency is asserted.
links.caveats: Functional requirement, not a claim that the 1959 lecture personally transmitted the technique to Sanger.
links.timing: Established copying operation precedes its later assay use.

evidence.locator: p. 441, Introduction and Principle of the Method
evidence.supports: Template copying is the implemented operation.

links.statement: Sanger and Coulson’s plus/minus sequencing method used DNA polymerase I as a synthesis reagent.
links.scope: Only the identified configurations and source-described contribution.
links.alternatives: No unique historical route or universal necessity asserted.
links.caveats: Enzyme-class capability is the source referent. No use of Kornberg’s original physical preparation or unique transmission route is asserted.
links.timing: The enzyme-preparation capability is recorded by 1957, before the 1975 published method.

evidence.locator: Principle of the method, printed pp. 442–443
evidence.supports: Explicit use of DNA polymerase I in the described method.
